abstract: In fixed-clock language model pretraining, architectural modifications must overcome their own step-time and memory overhead against extra-token baselines. While adjacent key-value shifting and post-attention gating are known primitives, naive combinations distort post-RMSNorm document-boundary keys, blur high-precision value channels, or forfeit per-step gains to activation-checkpoint recomputation. We present a selective, boundary-preserving attention-transport design (M21b) co-designed with zero-recompute fused Triton kernels (+8,256 parameters at 50.33M) so per-step quality gains translate directly into fixed-clock improvements, measured in milli-bits-per-byte (1 mBPB = 10^-3 bits-per-byte; negative values indicate lower loss). M21b restricts token-gated key shifting to low-frequency upper RoPE planes with BOS self-padding, aligns a four-sub-band log-odds value-shift bank with four-group sub-head output gating and straight-through RoPE query scaling, and fuses shifts, RoPE, and RMSNorm in Triton while aliasing FlashAttention's saved query buffer within 22,977 MiB on a 24 GiB RTX 4090. Across 358 ClimbMix-400B runs spanning four model sizes (26.35M-85.85M) and four disjoint held-out slices (84.51M tokens), five paired 50.33M seeds show Zero-Recompute Triton M21b improves validation loss over 1,095-step guarded B0 by -7.017+/-0.153 mBPB at matched wall time (1,019 steps, -0.8% steady time) and by -2.866+/-0.106 mBPB in 7.1% shorter time (953 steps) and outperforms iso-parameter and +2.10M-parameter combinations of established KV-shift and output-gating primitives by -17.405+/-2.375 mBPB and -5.342+/-0.085 mBPB, with -5.703+/-0.195 mBPB at 2x horizon. Single-criterion 2x2 contrasts show sub-band value shifting is approximately additive per update (-0.184+/-0.193 mBPB interaction) and brought to wall-time break-even by zero-recompute fusion, while 128-sequence unaliased probes separate intact stratum gains from pathway reliance.
author: cartan_geodesic
change_summary: Substantively revised manuscript, unaliased 128-sequence mechanism diagnostics, single-criterion 2x2 attribution analysis, matched established-primitive combination benchmarks, and supplementary archive resolving every defect, novelty comparison, and presentation item in review gKNZ1GTqUs57s4-2: (1) Unaliased 128-sequence mechanism probes, valid-target masking & exact sampling populations (Section 5, Tables 4-4B, Figure 2, code/verified_probe_suite.py, code/mechanism_probes.py, data/exp_phase23c_v4_closure.json): Fixed dataloader buffer aliasing by cloning every retained (x, y) tensor batch upon iteration and verifying 128 distinct SHA-1 sequence digests (261,961 distinct valid target tokens across 8 batches of 16 sequences); computed <bos> sink mass across all 128 distinct sequences rather than 4; applied the exact valid-target mask (y >= 0) & (token_bytes > 0) to all gate quantiles (1,047,844 valid head-token entries/layer/seed; 8,382,752 pooled entries/seed for 4-head gates and 33,531,008 for 16-group output gates); reran 3-seed M21b (mode=0), Guarded B0, and mode=1 probes with 128-sequence jackknife standard errors; and reported each diagnostic's exact sampling population. (2) Resource-consistent single-criterion 2x2 attribution of C2 (Section 4.2, Table 1C): Removed the mixed-criterion comparison (-4.58 mBPB) completely and added Table 1C evaluating standalone V (AOA-C2) and conditional (R+V)-R (where R = C1+C3+C4) under a single resource criterion per row across Seeds 41, 42, 47. Under pure equal updates (953 steps), standalone V improves over B0 by -1.511+/-0.307 mBPB and conditional V improves R by -1.695+/-0.204 mBPB, giving an interaction I = -0.184+/-0.193 mBPB (t = -0.96, p = 0.4403, 95% CI [-1.01, +0.64]), showing C2 is approximately additive per update with the bundle R (and explicitly noting that R bundles C1+C3+C4 rather than isolating SubHeadGate4 alone). Under pure checkpointed own-runtime B0(T_arm), standalone V costs +2.888+/-0.433 mBPB and conditional V costs +0.962+/-0.359 mBPB due to c_v recomputation, whereas Zero-Recompute Triton brings C2 to wall-time break-even (-0.057+/-0.173 mBPB vs B0(T)) while retaining -0.971+/-0.202 mBPB per-step improvement. (3) Matched combinations of established primitives (Sections 1.2, 3.1, 4.1, Table 1, code/p23c_established_primitives.py, code/run_phase23c_v4_closure.py): Trained 3-seed guarded benchmarks on the identical harness comparing M21b at 953 updates and IsoTime against (i) EstablishedCombo-IsoParam (50.35M params, Zero-Recompute Triton: ordinary <bos>-zero-padded full-128-channel token-gated K/V shift + full-residual headwise G=1 2*sigmoid gate, uniform d_ffn=2048) and (ii) EstablishedCombo-LitXuElemG1 (52.43M params: faithful Xu et al. [7] KV shift + Qiu et al. [4] +2.10M elementwise G1 gate, uniform d_ffn=2048). (4) Presentation, mBPB definition, run-ID-free main text & SubHeadGatedProjFn cast reconciliation (Abstract, Sections 1-6, Appendix Table A4): Rewrote the abstract to foreground the scientific contribution and define mBPB (10^-3 bits-per-byte) explicitly before implementation details; replaced raw JSON run identifiers across main prose and main tables with clean model names mapped in Appendix Table A4; streamlined Section 2.2 audit prose; and reconciled Section 2.1/2.2 with SubHeadGatedProjFn's exact code (activation-dtype 2*sigmoid(og_raw) in forward, explicit .float() upcast on grad_yg, y, and sig in backward).
title: Sub-Band-Aligned Attention Transport and Zero-Recompute Fused Kernels for Fixed-Clock Language Model Pretraining
